status: device-restored-from-native-evidence; st_w_04_03 compiles for 2-8 players once registered

binary.note: Read-only static disassembly via tools/capstone. No native code executed, no original asset shipped.

keyFinding.noDedicatedComponent: There is NO SwitchTimerComponent and NO SwitchTimerObserver anywhere in the binary. quantum-method-index.json only holds SwitchTimerActorComponent (a different actor type, used by st_w_14_04), and assembly-csharp-method-index.json only holds SwitchTimerActorView / EditableSwitchTimer*. The SwitchTimer actor is served by the shared Quantum TimerComponent.
keyFinding.proof: TimerComponent.ParseParameter 0x18172dd1b..0x18172dd47 switches on QActorCreateParam.type: 0x0a -> word[component+0]=0x102, 0x1f -> 0x101, 0x25 -> 0x103. installed-stage-decoded.local.json maps type 0x0a (10) to DeadTimer and type 0x25 (37) to SwitchTimer; type 0x1f (31) appears in no shipped stage. The low byte is m_TimeUpType, the high byte m_Type (il2cpp offsets 16 and 17), so a SwitchTimer is permanently TimerTimeUpType.Switch(3) + TimerType.TimeDown(1).
keyFinding.enumValues: quantum-field-offsets.json: TimerTimeUpType = None 0, Retry 1, Dead 2, Switch 3; TimerType = TimeUp 0, TimeDown 1.

quantumComponent.Creator: 0x18172d630
quantumComponent.InitCollision: absent - TimerComponent has no collision and no OnCollided at all

view.OnInitialize: 0x1805d1740 (hide test at 0x1805d189c: `test byte[component+2],1; ja` skips the whole UI build)

componentFieldOffsets.note: il2cpp offsets from quantum-field-offsets.json minus the 16 byte header; the module header quotes the same table.

flagBits.source: The bitfield uses the shared 16 bit QFlags instantiation (typeIndex 28513, also used by ThunderComponent, CountUpTimerComponent and others), so the bit NAMES are not in global-metadata.dat. The names below are derived from behaviour, the addresses are exact.
flagBits.bit0_hidden: ParseParameter 0x18172de41..0x18172de53 sets it from datas[13]. TimerComponent.IsVisible 0x1816b9070 returns !bit0, and TimerView.OnInitialize 0x1805d189c refuses to build the readout when it is set.
flagBits.bit1_muteTick: ParseParameter 0x18172de58..0x18172de6d sets it from datas[14]. OnUpdate 0x18172dfde skips Frame.PlaySe when it is set.
flagBits.bit2_stopped: OnUpdate 0x18172df48 (TimeDown) and 0x18172df0b (TimeUp) skip the ageing. Set by OnRecvEvent 0x18172e35e, cleared by OnRecvEvent 0x18172e327.
flagBits.bit3_firedTimeUp: Set after onTimeUp at 0x18172e03a, tested at 0x18172e00e and 0x18172e34f, cleared by ParseParameter 0x18172dd08 and SetSec 0x18172e3c9.

constants.UI_POSY: 0x01a00000 = 416, written at .cctor 0x18172e4fb (statics+0x18). Independently cross-checks the +416 readout anchor source-gate-devices.js already uses for SwitchObserver.
constants.timeUpEpsilon: OnUpdate 0x18172e008 `cmp rcx,4` on abs(m_Sec raw) - the same 4/65536 FP non-zero epsilon the Thunder and BlinkBlock ports already quote
constants.secondBias: OnUpdate 0x18172dfc5/0x18172dfcc `add rbx,-0x28f` then `sar ..,0x10` - 0x28f = 655 raw = ~0.009994 s, applied to the old AND the new value before the floor

supportingCalls.nameLookup: Frame.NotifyEvent 0x181749fa0 -> ActorSceneComponent.FindActor 0x1816a7b80: an EXACT-name dictionary hit that returns a single actor, and returns null for an empty name (0x1816a7c47 `cmp word[name],0`). Not prefix matching - unlike the SwitchObserver name filter in source-gate-devices.js.
supportingCalls.eventDelivery: NotifyEvents.Invoke_OnRecvEvent 0x18174a0a5 is called synchronously from inside onTimeUp, so the target reacts in the same frame
supportingCalls.eventParam: ActorComponent.GetEventParam 0x18169dbd0 -> QEventParamManager.Get 0x181780b80, which zeroes the entire param object (including +0x60 at 0x181780c29) before stamping the event id at +0x10 and the sender at +0x18
supportingCalls.eventPayloadMeaning: The +0x60 field a Timer reads for event 61 is filled by SwitchComponent.NotifyTarget 0x181714e06 from SwitchComponent.m_TimerAddSecond (il2cpp field offset 48 = struct +0x20, setter SetTimerAddSecond 0x18169cdf0), so the payload literally means 'seconds to add to a timer'. WHICH authored Switch parameter writes m_TimerAddSecond was not traced - SwitchComponent has no ParseParameter of its own.
supportingCalls.deltaTime: Frame.get_DeltaTime 0x18173a090 only forwards a runtime session field, so the FP raw of a native tick delta is NOT in the binary

dataSlotMap.0: m_Sec base, seconds (FP). Read at ParseParameter 0x18172d859..0x18172d866 and used as the running total `rbx`.
dataSlotMap.1: Per-player seconds. ParseParameter 0x18172da42..0x18172da4e: when datas[1] != FP._0 the base becomes `playerCount * datas[1] + datas[0]` (int * FP product on the raw). Zero in every shipped SwitchTimer.
dataSlotMap.2: m_Pos.x offset: m_Pos.x = UI_POSX(0) + datas[2]. Written at 0x18172dd6d..0x18172dd8a. UI only.
dataSlotMap.3: m_Pos.y offset: m_Pos.y = UI_POSY(416) + datas[3]. Same instruction block. UI only.
dataSlotMap.4: m_Scale factor: m_Scale = datas[4] * UI_BASE_SCALE(10), but ONLY when datas[4] > FP._0 (0x18172ddb5 `cmp rdi,[rax]; jle`), otherwise m_Scale stays 0. UI only.
dataSlotMap.5: m_TargetName, a QStringUtf8_32 built at 0x18172de29. This is the EVENT TARGET actor name, not a switch name filter: onTimeUp hands it to Frame.NotifyEvent, which does an exact-name single-actor lookup. In st_w_04_03 it names the Bridge actors.
dataSlotMap.6..12: Per-player-count override of m_Sec. ParseParameter 0x18172da58..0x18172dc5b: index = 6 + clamp(playerCount-2, 0, 7); a non-zero float there REPLACES everything computed from datas[0]/datas[1] (`test rax,rax; cmovne rbx,rax` at 0x18172da90). Counts 2..8 reach datas[6..12]. No shipped SwitchTimer populates any of them.
dataSlotMap.13: DUAL USE. (a) m_Flags bit0 = hide the timer UI, read as floor(raw) != 0 at 0x18172d9ab..0x18172d9c0 and applied at 0x18172de41. (b) It is also index 13 of the override table above, which the clamp only selects at 9 or more players - unreachable in PICO PARK 2, so in practice it is the hide flag only. This collision is in the original, not in the port.
dataSlotMap.14: m_Flags bit1 = mute the per-second Se. floor(raw) != 0, read at 0x18172d9cf..0x18172d9f4, applied at 0x18172de58.
dataSlotMap.15..18: Read ONLY when QActorCreateParam.type == 0x0a (DeadTimer): the guard at ParseParameter 0x18172da97 `cmp dword[createParam+0x30],0xa; jne 0x18172dcef` skips the whole QPlayerCountParamUtility.Find 0x181786950 block for a SwitchTimer. The module reports a warning if a SwitchTimer populates them.
dataSlotMap.19..31: Never read by ParseParameter for any Timer actor type.

behaviour.direction: Always TimerType.TimeDown for a SwitchTimer. OnUpdate 0x18172df57..0x18172df79: m_Sec -= Frame.DeltaTime, clamped to exactly 0 when the subtraction goes negative. (The TimeUp branch at 0x18172deff adds instead and returns immediately, so a count-up timer never reaches the time-up test - documented for completeness, unreachable here.)
behaviour.pause: m_Flags bit2 skips only the decrement. The per-second Se block and the time-up test still run every update, because 0x18172df4c jumps past the subtraction to 0x18172df81.
behaviour.tickSound: Only for m_TimeUpType Dead(2) or Switch(3) (0x18172df81 `movzx eax,byte[rsi]; sub al,2; cmp al,1; ja`). Fires when the new m_Sec < WARNING_SECOND(10), floor(sec - 655/65536) differs between the old and the new value, and bit1 is clear. The 0x28f bias puts each beep ~0.01 s past the round number and makes the `< 10` gate swallow the first crossing, so a 10 second warning beeps ten times at ~9.01, 8.01 .. 0.01 s remaining.
behaviour.timeUp: OnUpdate 0x18172dff6..0x18172e047: when abs(m_Sec) < 4/65536 and bit3 is clear, onTimeUp runs and bit3 is set, making it a one-shot for the rest of the stage.
behaviour.timeUpAction: onTimeUp 0x18172e0cb..0x18172e11d for TimerTimeUpType.Switch: GetEventParam(event 0x3d = 61), then Frame.NotifyEvent with m_TargetName. That is exactly the 'switch on' event source-gate-devices.js and source-bridge-devices.js already consume (61 on / 60 off). The payload field +0x60 is left at the 0 that QEventParamManager.Get wrote, so the event carries timerAddSecond 0. An empty m_TargetName silently reaches nobody.
behaviour.otherTimeUpActions: Retry(1) sets stage flag bit 10 at 0x18172e232; Dead(2) broadcasts event 0x13, plays an Se, clears stage flag bit 9 and starts StageNoticeComponent 0x18170e850. Neither is reachable from actor type 37, and neither is ported - the module throws if it ever sees them.
behaviour.incomingEvents: OnRecvEvent 0x18172e250 dispatches three ids and forwards everything else to ActorComponent.OnRecvEvent 0x18169e840. 61 while bit3 is clear: payload 0 -> set bit2 (stop); payload != 0 -> m_Sec = ceil-to-whole-second(m_Sec + payload) (0x18172e374 `test ax,ax` then `and rax,~0xffff; add rax,0x10000`) and fire FrameEvents.Timer_BeatAnimation. 60: clear bit2 unconditionally, even after time-up. 47 (0x2f): consumed by a log call, no state change.
behaviour.collision: None at all. No InitCollision, no OnCollided, no solid, no hazard, nothing to stand on. solids() is always empty.
behaviour.worldPosition: The authored posX/posY are irrelevant to the logic: ParseParameter never reads the actor transform, and the readout position comes from the UI statics plus datas[2]/datas[3]. st_w_04_03 places both timers at (0,0).

installedParameterSets.meaning: At 7 or 8 players only, two hidden and silent 3.5 second countdowns that each send event 61 to one of the two Bridge actors, which then extend from 1 to 7 segments. Below 7 players the timers do not exist, so those bridges never extend - Bridge1/Bridge2 have playerCount 0 and datas[6]=0 (no key trigger), and nothing else in the stage names them.
Visible, audible 30 second round timer at UI (0, 448) and scale 6; present in all seven variants of the stage.
Unnamed visible timers at the default UI anchor (0, 416) and scale 10. Because the actor name is empty they can never be addressed by an event themselves.

unresolved: Frame.DeltaTime's FP raw is not in the binary (Frame.get_DeltaTime 0x18173a090 forwards a runtime session field), so the exact tick a countdown expires on could not be verified. With FP delta raw 1092 (65536/60) a 3.5 s timer would expire on tick 211, while this port - ageing a float by the caller's seconds delta and using the native 4/65536 epsilon - expires on tick 210. One native tick of uncertainty, the same gap source-blink-devices.js already records.

The Quantum system update ORDER between TimerComponent.OnUpdate and BridgeComponent.OnUpdate was not recovered. The port emits the time-up event from beforeStep so the bridge starts extending on the same tick; the original could begin one tick earlier or later.

m_Flags bit NAMES are not recoverable: the field uses the shared 16 bit QFlags instantiation, so global-metadata.dat holds no per-bit identifiers. Bits 0-3 are named from behaviour only; bits 4-15 are never touched by TimerComponent.

datas[1] (per-player seconds) and datas[6..12] (per-count override) are implemented from ParseParameter alone - no shipped SwitchTimer populates either, so only the synthetic probes in the test file exercise them.

The whole OnRecvEvent path (stop / resume / add-time) is implemented from the disassembly alone. No shipped actor sends an event to a SwitchTimer. The only shipped Timer that is addressed by name is DeadTimer1 in st_w_05_02, named by the datas[0] of 23 Switch actors, and that is actor type 10 - outside this module. Which Switch parameter supplies the m_TimerAddSecond payload was not traced, so the stop-versus-add branch is untested against shipped data.

Frame.GetPlayerActorCount 0x1817494b0 counts player actors in the scene, which is not provably identical to the Frame.GetPlayerIndexCount that drives actor population selection (population-rules.cjs). The port feeds it `count`. Since every shipped SwitchTimer has datas[1]=0 and an empty override table, the value has no observable effect on shipped data.
The ~0.01 s second bias (0x28f) is reproduced exactly, but it only affects when the tick Se plays; no gameplay value depends on it.

The ceil-to-whole-second on add-time is computed by quantising the port's float seconds back to FP raw (round(v*65536)) before the native `and ~0xffff; add 0x10000`. That quantisation is the port's, not the original's.

SwitchTimerActor (st_w_14_04, SwitchTimerActorComponent, ParseParameter 0x18171a5a0) is a DIFFERENT actor type with a packed-table slot 0 and a target name in slot 1. It is not needed by st_w_04_03 and is NOT implemented here.

DeadTimer (type 10) would reuse this component but needs the Dead time-up branch, the QPlayerCountParamUtility.Find block for datas[15..18] and a stage-wide death request. Not implemented; the module throws rather than guessing.

api.create(compiled): {count, ticks, timers:[{sec, stopped, firedTimeUp, tickSound, timeUp, beat, ...}]}
api.beforeStep(state, {dt}): ages every timer and returns {events, sounds, solids:[]}; events are the time-up event 61 notifications
api.afterStep(state, {events}): drains incoming events through signal() and returns {events:[], deadPlayerIds:[], hazards:[], solids:[]}
api.signal(state, event): applies one incoming event (61 stop/add-time, 60 resume, 47 ignored); returns whether any timer matched
api.displays(state): readout rows for the non-hidden timers (mm:ss, UI position, scale, warning flag)
api.nativeConstants: uiBaseScale, uiPosX, uiPosY, warningSecond, tickSeId, fpEpsilon, seSecondBias, eventOn, eventOff, actorType, timeUpType, timerType

tests.data: Real extracted actors from installed-stage-decoded.local.json (st_w_04_03, st_b_01_09, st_b_01_03, plus a sweep over every variant of all five stages that contain a SwitchTimer). verification.scratchRegistration: The nine edits below were applied to a copy of source-stage-runtime.js under the session scratchpad (scratch-stage-runtime.js), never to the repository file.
verification.compileMatrix: st_w_04_03 compiles for 2,3,4,5,6,7,8 players: 0 timers at 2-6, 2 timers at 7 and 8. The seven other stages the runtime whitelists (st_w_01_01..st_w_01_04, st_w_04_01, st_w_04_04, st_w_10_02) still compile for 2-8 with 0 timers.
verification.pipelineProbe: With the scratch registration, a 7 player st_w_04_03 session leaves both bridges at phase 0 for 209 ticks and starts both extending on tick 210, the tick both timers reach zero; at 6 players they never move. (The shipped stage kills an idle party in ~1.4 s, so the probe forces the death state back to play - it is a plumbing check, not a playthrough.)
verification.notModified: source-stage-runtime.js, package-source-play.cjs, deploy-source-play.cjs, play/, every existing source-*-devices.js and deploy-chamchicode/ are untouched.

registration.note: source-stage-runtime.js was NOT modified. Apply these nine edits; every quoted find string is unique in the file as of commit e8488b4ad117f2386fc0fa84fe92ea555280ac03.

edits.comment: Age the timers at the very top of tick() and hand the time-up events to every module that owns a possible target, so a Bridge starts extending on the same tick the timer expires. Gates.signal and Devices.signal are the per-event entry points those modules already expose.
Let the timers receive the relay and device events of the tick (stop / resume / add-time), next to where Bridges already consumes them.

registration.alreadyWhitelisted: st_w_04_03 is already in the stage whitelist on line 20, so no edit is needed there.
registration.optional: SwitchTimers.displays(s.switchTimerState) can feed a timer readout. st_w_04_03 needs none: both of its timers set the hide flag.
